# Built-in profiles

Profiles snug ships. Each section is the output of `snug profile show NAME`.
`snug --dry-run -p NAME DIR` shows what one produces for a directory.

Every run starts with `@sys` `@home` `@target-rw`, unless `config.toml` or
`--no-defaults` changes that. See [Selecting profiles](configuration.md#selecting-profiles).

## `@claude`

```text
profile     @claude
            Claude Code: binary and skills read-only, credentials projected and settings generated.
defined in  builtin:base.toml

  includes         @sys
                   @home
  ro               {home}/.local/bin/claude:/snug/bin/claude
                   {home}/.local/share/claude
                   {home}/.claude/skills
                   {home}/.claude/plugins
  environ.inherit  ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL  ← every request the agent makes, conversation included, goes to this endpoint instead of Anthropic's (documented, not measured on this host)
                   NO_COLOR
                   PAGER  ← the value is a command; git runs it over log, diff and show via GIT_PAGER -> core.pager -> PAGER (measured)
  optional         {home}/.local/bin/claude {home}/.local/share/claude {home}/.claude/skills {home}/.claude/plugins

To see what this actually produces for a directory:
  snug --dry-run -p @claude <dir>
```

## `@git`

```text
profile     @git
            Your git name and email, extracted from the host config. Generated, never bound.
defined in  builtin:base.toml

  git              extract
                   ~/.gitconfig is REGENERATED from a whitelist, never bound -
                   it names programs git would run

To see what this actually produces for a directory:
  snug --dry-run -p @git <dir>
```

## `@home`

```text
profile     @home
            $HOME is an empty tmpfs at the host path. Writable, ephemeral.
defined in  builtin:base.toml

  tmpfs            {home}
                   {home}/.cache
                   {home}/.config
                   {home}/.local/state
                   {home}/.local/share
  environ.set      XDG_CACHE_HOME = {home}/.cache
                   XDG_CONFIG_HOME = {home}/.config
                   XDG_DATA_HOME = {home}/.local/share
                   XDG_STATE_HOME = {home}/.local/state

To see what this actually produces for a directory:
  snug --dry-run -p @home <dir>
```

## `@net`

```text
profile     @net
            Internet access via a private network namespace. Host loopback unreachable.
defined in  builtin:base.toml

  network          egress
                   the sandbox reaches the whole internet, from a private netns.
                   Host loopback and abstract unix sockets stay unreachable
                   (pathname sockets — X11, D-Bus — are a mount question,
                   not this one).
  dns              yes
                   a generated /etc/resolv.conf names a resolver inside the
                   sandbox

To see what this actually produces for a directory:
  snug --dry-run -p @net <dir>
```

## `@podman-build`

```text
profile     @podman-build
            As podman-socket, plus `podman build` with a filtered option set.
defined in  builtin:base.toml

  includes         @podman-socket
  podman           build
                   starts a container engine and delegates your whole subuid
                   range, even with no network profile selected

To see what this actually produces for a directory:
  snug --dry-run -p @podman-build <dir>
```

## `@podman-socket`

```text
profile     @podman-socket
            Containers via a filtering proxy over a per-sandbox podman engine, offline unless @net is also selected.
defined in  builtin:base.toml

  includes         @sys
                   @home
  ro               /etc/containers
  podman           socket
                   starts a container engine and delegates your whole subuid
                   range, even with no network profile selected
  optional         /etc/containers

To see what this actually produces for a directory:
  snug --dry-run -p @podman-socket <dir>
```

## `@sys`

```text
profile     @sys
            Read-only OS runtime: /usr plus the few /etc files things actually need.
defined in  builtin:base.toml

  ro               /usr
                   /opt
                   /etc/ld.so.cache
                   /etc/ld.so.conf
                   /etc/ld.so.conf.d
                   /etc/ssl
                   /etc/pki
                   /etc/ca-certificates
                   /etc/ca-certificates.conf
                   /etc/crypto-policies
                   /var/lib/ca-certificates
                   /usr/share/ca-certificates
                   /etc/localtime
                   /etc/os-release
                   /etc/alternatives
                   /etc/services
                   /etc/protocols
  symlink          /bin -> usr/bin
                   /sbin -> usr/sbin
                   /lib -> usr/lib
                   /lib64 -> usr/lib64
  nss              yes
                   generated /etc/passwd, /etc/group and /etc/nsswitch.conf name
                   the host login name, uid, primary gid and group name —
                   already exposed by `id` and $USER — and nothing else; no
                   other account, no member list, no command table
  optional         /opt /etc/ld.so.conf.d /etc/ssl /etc/pki /etc/ca-certificates /etc/ca-certificates.conf /etc/crypto-policies /var/lib/ca-certificates /usr/share/ca-certificates /etc/localtime /etc/os-release /etc/alternatives /etc/services /etc/protocols

To see what this actually produces for a directory:
  snug --dry-run -p @sys <dir>
```

## `@target-rw`

```text
profile     @target-rw
            The target directory is writable and persists.
defined in  builtin:base.toml

  includes         @home
  rw               {target}

To see what this actually produces for a directory:
  snug --dry-run -p @target-rw <dir>
```
